summary: You carry a quiet doubt about whether you're enough, even when there's no reason for it. Who you are and what you fear you're not pull against each other, so you may overwork to prove it, or hold yourself back before anyone else can.
body: You carry a quiet doubt about whether you're enough, even when there's no reason for it. Who you are and what you fear you're not pull against each other, so you may overwork to prove it, or hold yourself back before anyone else can. Approval may not feel automatic. It can feel tied to effort, restraint, or the sense that respect has to be earned over time. You're often a late bloomer who grows into real authority with age. The work is building self-respect from the inside instead of waiting for someone to grant it.
gift: At your best: self-made, credible, the kind of authority that's actually earned.
shadow: The trap: harsh self-judgment, and waiting for a permission that never comes.
integration: Let responsibility become a path to self-respect, not a verdict on your value. You are allowed to grow into authority without carrying every old standard forward.
do: Define enough on your own terms
Build self-respect instead of waiting to be granted it
Let yourself be a late bloomer
dont: Hold back to avoid being judged
